R016-01.notes: Para 2: color vision needs several cell types; octopus has one. Para 4: blur differences let it infer color through optics 'what its retina cannot detect.' A synthesizes both.

flags: minor: R016-01 and R016-02 both test the pupil/chromatic-blur idea in para 4; mild overlap but neither gives away the other's key

flags: minor: key reuses para 2 wording 'each tuned to a different range of wavelengths', a lift test-wise students can match to the stated weakness of the skin proposal
R016-03.notes: Para 3 limitation: skin proteins seem to be a single type, so they may not sense color. Multiple tuned types would address that. A concerns speed, not color; C is the pupil proposal; D concerns texture in darkness.

flags: minor: 'the puzzle may matter less for survival' is a somewhat abstract paraphrase; the passage's point is that exact color matching may not be needed, which C captures only loosely, though no rival choice is defensible
R016-04.notes: Para 5: matching brightness and texture may be enough against predators that see color poorly. A, B, D are unsupported or contradicted ('Neither proposal has been confirmed').

flags: minor: key is a direct paraphrase of 'no better than chance'; pure detail retrieval

flags: minor: distractors are easy to eliminate (A contradicts 'neither proposal has been confirmed'; C and D are off topic)
R016-07.notes: The passage presents the colorblind-camouflage puzzle, then the skin, pupil and no-need-to-match explanations.

R016-08.notes: Para 2: experience depends 'at least as much' on feel as on length. Time matters (half true), but so do uncertainty, fairness and similar factors.
